  • It has been revealed that others might have crumbled.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his fresh club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

It has been revealed that others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

Industry observers note that as for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

Recent findings suggest that all that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In a recent development, in the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN.

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

Industry observers note that “It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

In a recent development, “After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

Recent findings suggest that “It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”.

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0.

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr.

Sources indicate that “I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”.

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We revealed our quality today. The result reflected that.”.

On his relationship with Kai Havertz:.

Sources indicate that “He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”.

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. Bukayo Saka has arrived at a career crossroads. We will soon learn whether he is destined to be a good Arsenal player or if he will elevate himself to the level of Premier League, Champions League and England great.

This weekend Saka turns 25, an age when footballers typically enter their peak. Although his legendary status at Arsenal is secure as a title winner, the reaction to the champions’ transfer window suggests there is a general feeling that he can and should produce more to earn “world class” status.

Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta is short of such an attacker. He spent the summer investigating whether players of Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez’s calibre might add much-needed stardust to his front three. Failure to secure a major-name forward has led many to conclude that Arsenal’s title defence will be in the mould of their impressive, but cautious 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

"It's another tough game"Ben White on coming up against Chelsea's front three 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/gfazGGNSA8.

Sources indicate that it is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

In a recent development, “This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once noted of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”.

How chaotic will Arsenal allow the game to become today? Both of Chelsea’s league matches this season have been remarkably open, to the point of silliness. Arsenal do not usually allow such things to happen on their watch. They are far too sensible for that. But, having seen Brighton create so many chances at Stamford Bridge last week, Arteta may fancy his team to do some serious damage to Chelsea’s damage if the match opens up.

In a recent development, there’s a slight surprise in Chelsea’s line-up with Levi Colwill dropping to the bench and Josh Acheampong coming in. That could point to Alonso changing to a back four with Acheampong at right-back and Pedro Neto playing further forwards as a right winger. In a recent development, mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

In a recent development, “We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very vital.”.

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

It’s very notable to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”.

  • Un numero significativo soprattutto se rapportato a quanto accadeva dodici mesi fa.
  • Sources indicate that entrando nel dettaglio della stagione 2026/27, il Girone A conta sei avvicendamenti: Carpi, Dolomiti Bellunesi, Folgore Caratese, Giana Erminio, Novara e Renate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in Serie C, il valzer delle panchine che non accenna a fermarsi. Anzi, rispetto alla passata stagione, il ritmo degli avvicendamenti sembra essersi ulteriormente intensificato. L'ultimo aggiornamento, con il Carpi che ha salutato Stefano Cassani per affidarsi ad Alessandro Miramari e il Forlì che, dopo le dimissioni di Nicola Campedelli, ha scelto Lamberto Zauli, porta infatti a 20 il numero delle squadre che hanno già cambiato guida tecnica dall'inizio del campionato. Un dato che comprende 19 esoneri e un addio volontario, quello del tecnico dei romagnoli.

Un numero significativo soprattutto se rapportato a quanto accadeva dodici mesi fa. Il 18 novembre 2025, alla stessa altezza della stagione, le squadre che avevano già effettuato almeno un cambio in panchina erano infatti 12. Otto in meno rispetto alla fotografia attuale, con un incremento del 66,7%.

Sources indicate that entrando nel dettaglio della stagione 2026/27, il Girone A conta sei avvicendamenti: Carpi, Dolomiti Bellunesi, Folgore Caratese, Giana Erminio, Novara e Renate. Nel Girone B il conto sale a sette con Forlì, Gubbio, Guidonia Montecelio, Pineto, Sambenedettese, Vado e Vis Pesaro. Altri sette cambi anche nel Girone C, dove sono state coinvolte Altamura, Casarano, Casertana, Giugliano, Picerno, Salernitana e Scafatese.

According to recent reports, un anno fa, invece, al 18 novembre la situazione era decisamente diversa. Nel Girone A erano quattro le società ad aver cambiato allenatore: Arzignano Valchiampo, Dolomiti Bellunesi, Lumezzane e Triestina. Tre nel Girone B, ovvero Livorno, Perugia e Torres, mentre il Girone C faceva registrare cinque avvicendamenti con Benevento, Foggia, Giugliano, Picerno e Sorrento. Dodici in totale, dunque, contro le venti attuali.

Il confronto diventa ancora più interessante se si allarga lo sguardo all'intera stagione 2025/26. Al termine del campionato, infatti, erano state ben 24 le squadre, sulle 60 partecipanti, ad aver vissuto almeno un cambio in panchina. Nove nel Girone A, sette nel Girone B e otto nel Girone C.

According to recent reports, non sono mancati nemmeno i casi di particolare instabilità. Basti pensare al Giugliano, che nel corso dell'annata ha attraversato sei diverse gestioni tecniche, considerando anche i periodi affidati a Luca Tulino ad interim. Situazione movimentata anche al Foggia e alla Sambenedettese, entrambe passate attraverso cinque differenti incarichi in panchina, contando anche i ritorni e le soluzioni temporanee.

It has been revealed that la stagione in corso, dunque, ha già raggiunto l'83% del numero di società che avevano cambiato allenatore nell'intero campionato precedente. Un raffronto che, pur considerando come il percorso del 2026/27 sia ancora lungo e che non tutti gli avvicendamenti siano riconducibili a esoneri in senso stretto, fotografa una tendenza evidente: in Serie C la pazienza delle società nei confronti dei propri allenatori sembra essere sempre più limitata. E il conto, con ancora gran parte del campionato da disputare, è inevitabilmente destinato a rimanere aperto.

Una posizione più arretrata a centrocampo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La conferenza stampa di Gennaro Gattuso in occasione della sfida casalinga contro il Lecce.

La sosta per gli impegni delle nazionali è finalmente giunta al termine, e le squadre di Serie A sono pronte a scendere in campo per la dodicesima giornata. In occasione del prossimo turno, la Lazio ospiterà allo stadio Olimpico di Roma il Lecce di Di Francese per la sfida in programma sabato 21 novembre alle ore 15:00. Dalla sala stampa del Training Center di Formello, il mister Gattuso è intervenuto in conferenza stampa per presentare il match contro i salentini.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Su Frattesi non devo riflettere, ha fatto tutto col gruppo, sta bene e a livello strumentale non ha nulla. Se oggi arriva e ha il raffreddore vediamo, ma ha fatto tutto. Isaksen e Provstgaard hanno fatto un lavoro in palestra come Dele-Bashiru e Belahyane. Tutti i giocatori hanno lavorato con noi. Zaccagni sta lavorando sul campo, c’è ancora un po’ di edema, ma riesce a gestire. Nuno ha cominciato riabilitazione in piscina con Sutalo. Marusic ha avuto una piccola ricaduta, sulla ricaduta che ha avuto un mese fa. Settimana prossima valutiamo in che condizione sono. Gli altri sono tutti a disposizione. Cataldi ieri non si è allenato, ha avuto un piccolo problema all’adduttore, ma pensiamo non sia nulla di grave.

Si pensa a domani, non a quello che dobbiamo fare dopo. Giochiamo contro una squadra solida e allenata bene, ha dieci punti in classifica. Ha vinto con l’Udinese e col Venezia, una squadra molto insidiosa sui calci piazzati. Dobbiamo prenderli con le pinze. Sta a noi come sempre. Servirà mentalità e voglia di stare in campo e giocare a ritmi elevati. È una partita molto difficile.

Ci può stare, ma per come giochiamo il modulo non c’entra niente. Dipende solo come andare a prendere gli avversari in pressing. L’importante è andare a occupare le posizioni libere, cambia poco. Conta la voglia, la partecipazione e la mentalità. Per questo, si può fare tutto, se andate a vedere quando facciamo pressioni stiamo solo con un vertice. Conta poco il modulo.

Non devo entrare solo nella sua, devo entrare nella testa di tutti. Lui è un giocatore importante ma ci sono anche gli altri. Bisogna capire cosa significa giocare poco. Sia Dele-Bashiru e Lazzari ci danno sempre un contributo quando entrano. Albert quando sta bene è un giocatore di altissimo livello. Domani tanti di loro che hanno trovato poco spazio avranno la possibilità di giocare dal primo minuto, ma sono tranquillo. L’importante è avere la consapevolezza che i giocatori hanno una buona condizione.

According to recent reports, per come sono fatto io non sono mai sereno, fa parte del mio modo di essere. Ho la consapevolezza che sono ragazzi che non si risparmiano mai. La qualità di corsa è alta, sono tutti ad un ottimo livello e questo mi riempie d’orgoglio. Domani dovremo far parlare in campo e metterlo in pratica.

Quando ho detto che non abbiamo niente da perdere mi hanno guardato storto, ma altri ragionamenti si fanno nelle ultime partite. Noi dobbiamo vivere partita dopo partita. Giochiamocela domani, poi vedremo dove si arriva. Io alleno una squadra che in questo momento deve vivere alla giornata. Le partite bisogna giocarle, importante è che non sbagliamo a livello di atteggiamento.

According to recent reports, ieri abbiamo visto la partita contro il Napoli, serve la mentalità, il guardarsi. Il veleno su ogni palla, quello deve essere nel nostro DNA. Siamo andati là e potevamo fare più di un gol, poi nel primo quarto d’ora potevamo perderla, poi siamo tornati in partita. Non bisogna dimenticare cosa ci ha portato qui. Jude Bellingham sealed England's stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain with a kiss from girlfriend Ashlyn Castro as the couple made a rare public appearance together on Sunday.

England, who romped to a 3-0 lead with a superb display before the hour mark, were forced to weather a late onslaught from the Spanish after Elliot Anderson was shown a red card in the 63rd minute of the Nations League clash.

Although Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams managed to claw two back for this year's World Cup winners, England held on with a backs-to-the-wall effort in the closing stages, courtesy of a few fine saves from Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford.

After England's victory, which called an end to Spain's historic 43-game unbeaten run, Bellingham was spotted celebrating with his model girlfriend Ashlyn inside the stadium.

Wearing a beaming smile, he went over to embrace both the 28-year-old American and his father Mark as the family soaked up the celebrations in the stands.

The Real Madrid superstar has largely kept his relationship with Ashlyn private since the pair were first linked in early 2025.

Jude Bellingham and his girlfriend Ashlyn Castro celebrate England's superb win over Spain.

The Real Madrid star then caught up with his dad Mark on a special night for the Bellinghams.

Ashlyn is a model and social media influencer from California (@instagram/ashlyncastro).

Ashlyn is a model and social media influencer from California who boasts over one million followers on Instagram, sharing fashion and beauty content online.

Spanish media waxed lyrical about Bellingham's display on the night, claiming he was 'determined to make a statement' at the stadium of Real Madrid's rivals Atletico.

Newspaper AS wrote: 'If anyone felt the match was crucial, it was Jude Bellingham. He stepped onto the Metropolitano pitch determined to make a statement, to impose his usual footballing and physical prowess.

'He exudes football in every movement, and his rise to the top is unstoppable.'.

It was a proud international break for the Bellinghams before a ball was kicked in Madrid, with Jude's 21-year-old younger brother Jobe also earning his first England call-up last week.

Jude and Jobe would have become the first brothers to play for England since Gary and Phil Neville 17 years ago, but the younger sibling stayed on Thomas Tuchel's bench as an unused substitute.

England, who topped Group C on goal difference over Spain, will now not play until the Nations League quarter-finals kick off next spring.

The final, should Tuchel's Three Lions make it that far, are scheduled for the summer.

Il doppio ex elogia la partenza della squadra di Gattuso e indica come il Lecce può cercare un risultato utile all’Olimpico.

Per Eugenio Fascetti, la Lazio è nettamente favorita contro il Lecce nella sfida di domani alle 15 all’Olimpico. Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta del Mezzogiorno, Il doppio ex, però, avverte che i giallorossi dovranno giocare tutte le proprie carte per cercare un risultato utile. Elogia inoltre l’avvio dei biancocelesti, pur indicando nell’Inter la sua favorita per lo scudetto.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that fascetti ha allenato il Lecce dalla stagione 1983/1984 alla 1985/1986. Con il presidente Franco Jurlano, il direttore sportivo Mimmo Cataldo e i calciatori della stagione 1984/1985 conquistò la prima promozione del club salentino in Serie A. Da giocatore aveva vestito anche la maglia della Lazio nel 1964/1965; dopo l’esperienza a Lecce, guidò i biancocelesti nel 1986/1987 e nel 1987/1988.

Sources indicate that A Roma ottenne prima la salvezza tra i cadetti, nonostante una penalizzazione iniziale di nove punti, poi la promozione in A. A 88 anni, dopo una vita trascorsa nel calcio tra campo e panchina, l’allenatore viareggino continua a seguire con attenzione la massima serie italiana e non solo.

Recent findings suggest that fascetti conserva un legame con entrambe le piazze: «Ho splendidi ricordi delle esperienze vissute in entrambe le piazze». Ripensando alla promozione leccese, aggiunge: «Due avventure che rammento con molto piacere. A Lecce, con un grande gruppo di lavoro, dalla dirigenza allo staff, dai calciatori ad ogni collaboratore, raggiungemmo un traguardo che tutti, nel Salento, sognavano. Fu una cavalcata straordinaria, come del resto i festeggiamenti di popolo che seguirono, coinvolgendo un intero territorio.».

Recent findings suggest that A quel traguardo Fascetti affianca il ricordo della morte di Michele Lorusso e Ciro Pezzella: «In giallorosso, purtroppo, ho vissuto anche un grave lutto, la tragica morte di Michele e di Ciro (le bandiere Lorusso e Pezzella ndr), che ancora oggi, a distanza di oltre 40 anni da quel maledetto 2 dicembre 1983, mi procura dolore solo a parlarne. Anche con la Lazio, però, ci siamo tolti delle belle soddisfazioni».

Nel giudizio di Fascetti, il percorso del Lecce rispecchia quello di una squadra chiamata a lottare fino alla fine per restare in Serie A: «Il Lecce sta effettuando il cammino che compete ad uno schieramento che ha l’obiettivo di lottare sino alla fine per cercare di meritare la permanenza». Sugli alti e bassi precisa: «Per le formazioni costruite per salvarsi, è scontato che vadano messi in conto degli alti e bassi. Non potrebbe essere diversamente. I giallorossi sono in linea con le aspettative e dovranno battagliare con i denti per provare a compiere l’ennesima impresa sportiva degli ultimi anni. La sofferenza fa parte del dna degli appassionati salentini».

Sources indicate that il presidente Saverio Sticchi Damiani e gli altri soci cercano di conciliare i risultati con un calcio sostenibile e conti in ordine. Finora, secondo Fascetti, ci sono riusciti. L’ex tecnico considera questa strada necessaria per i club di provincia: «Per le piccole realtà di provincia non ci sono alternative».

Il paragone di Fascetti va alla gestione che conobbe a Lecce: «Ai miei tempi, Jurlano e Cataldo si sono dimostrati bravissimi a regalare a più riprese la serie A al Lecce a costi limitati. Due autentici campioni. L’attuale proprietà si muove lungo la medesima direttrice ed è la scelta giusta, anche se i tifosi, in quanto tali, vorrebbero soffrire di meno».

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window.
  • It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

It has been revealed that their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

Industry observers note that but here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

Sources indicate that "That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

“Brilliant technique,” remarked David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”.

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” remarked Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”.

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

In a recent development, how had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

Recent findings suggest that it could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

Recent findings suggest that when Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

In a recent development, his substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia.

Sources indicate that “I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes stated. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”.

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

Industry observers note that david Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Recent findings suggest that blerim Dzemaili, intervenuto a Radio Tutto Napoli, ha parlato di Dan Ndoye, esterno ora in forza al Nottingham Forest che però in passato è stato vicino all'Inter. Ecco le parole di Dzemaili: "Eravate vicini a uno dei giocatori che a me piacciono di più: Ndoye. Anche l'Inter era vicina. È un giocatore che ti fa spaccare le partite. Però il valore di mercato è altissimo. Una volta che sei in Premier League, anche se valevi 10 milioni, ne vali subito 40, perché in Premier le valutazioni purtroppo sono così. Anche se dovrebbero essere diverse, ma il calcio è così".

Secondo me il Napoli, se deve fare uno o due acquisti, deve sicuramente mettere sul tavolo più soldi del solito. Perché a gennaio, se vuoi davvero dei giocatori forti, devi spendere cifre diverse. Il mercato di gennaio è strano. Non so quanto abbia senso andare a spendere 30 o 40 milioni per un giocatore che magari poi non ti dà quello che ti aspetti e che sopravvaluti anche nell'acquisto, perché alla fine non vale tutti quei soldi. Per me ha più senso se l'allenatore conosce bene un giocatore e dice di volerlo perché può aiutarlo da subito fino a giugno. In quali ruoli ha bisogno il Napoli in questo momento? Penso a un attaccante, sicuramente, ma per me serve anche un leader difensivo che possa gestire tutta la squadra. Un leader difensivo".

England deliver the spectacular as Three Lions strip world champions Spain of their invincibility and give Thomas Tuchel the proof that his coaching IS working, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1483 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • In a recent development, thomas Tuchel had said he wanted evidence.
  • It has been revealed that he needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026.

In a recent development, thomas Tuchel had said he wanted evidence. He needed to believe his coaching was working. He needed to see something that told him he could help England overcome those DNA deficiencies he had identified in the aftermath of the devastating World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

It has been revealed that he needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best. He needed to cling on to the idea that they could overhaul Spain, that the work he was doing could improve England so much they could win the European Championship in 2028 and end this country’s cursed cycle of despair.

Proof of concept, he called it on Saturday night when England arrived in Madrid. ‘This will be proof of concept on the highest level,’ Tuchel predicted. ‘It's the biggest test in world football. Spain seems unbeatable but we are trying to take it away from them. We are up for something spectacular.’.

Sources indicate that something spectacular is what Tuchel promised and something spectacular is what both he and England delivered. Spain had not lost for 43 matches, a world record, but number 44 was beyond them. For just over an hour, England destroyed them. They outplayed them. They stripped them of their invincibility.

And then, when Elliot Anderson was sent off after 63 minutes for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Spain stormed back into the game, England somehow managed to hold on for a momentous victory in the screaming, yelling cauldron of the Metropolitano. This was proof alright. This was proof positive.

Industry observers note that sure, it was nervy for half an hour. And, yes, England nearly found a way to throw it away. But the way they played when it was 11 v 11 was enough for any England fan to believe that England under Tuchel can climb back to the summit of a major tournament and gaze down on a view they have not seen for 60 years.

England recorded a famous victory over Spain in Madrid as they won a five-goal thriller.

Elliot Anderson's red card opened the door for the world champions to mount a comeback.

James Trafford made a superb double save in stoppage time to preserve England's lead.

Yes, this was a Nations League dead rubber because both teams were already guaranteed progress to the quarter-finals next March, but there was no mistaking its wider significance. This was proof England are good enough to turn away from the trail of tears that has been their path for so long. Before the game, Spain had held the World Cup aloft again as one final reminder of England’s failure but by the end, by the time goalkeeper James Trafford had added to the drama with a miraculous double save, the glory and the 3-2 triumph was England’s.

Spain had won their last 12 matches in succession and the sport’s last two major tournament. They had not been beaten since March 2024 and had not lost at home since September 2022. England ended that run with 10 men. What a night. It was a special kind of crazy.

In a recent development, england had celebrated Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph and caps record at Wembley last week but Spain took things a stage further before the game. The boys who won the U15 World Cup were introduced to the crowd. Then the World Cup itself was carried on for goalkeeper Unai Simon to hold aloft.

According to recent reports, england ignored it all. They started the game like an express train. They nearly took the lead inside the first two minutes when Jude Bellingham met a corner from Declan Rice on the edge of the six-yard-box and was only denied by a brilliant reaction save from Simon. Gordon’s follow-up was destined for the bottom corner before it was blocked by a Spain defender.

It has been revealed that spain were rattled. The crowd whistled. England forced their opponents into mistake after mistake at the back. From one of those successful presses, Kane drilled a shot inches wide. Gordon, who has made such a fine start to his Barcelona career, revelled on the stage and caused right back Marc Pubill all manner of anxieties.

It has been revealed that spain could barely break out of their own half but when they did, after a quarter of an hour, Yamal ran at Lewis Hall and nutmegged him before Rice chopped the teenager down. Rice was booked by French referee Clement Turpin and Lamal windmilled his hands in the air to wind up the crowd.

In a recent development, pubill was replaced midway through the half. It looked like an injury but it could have been hurt pride or twisted blood. Gordon had barely given him a moment’s rest. In fact, Gordon was tireless. He harried Martin Zubimendi off the ball with ease and almost set up a chance for Bellingham.

England got the goal they deserved a minute before half-time. The build-up was controversial. Anderson played a fine through ball to Kane that doubled as a crunching tackle on Marc Cucurella. Cucurella went down as if he had been shot, which is what Cucurella always does.

Ben White slotted the ball through the keeper's legs after a brilliant England move.

Harry Kane celebrates goal No 93 for England after giving them the lead from the penalty spot.

It has been revealed that the referee allowed play to continue. Kane advanced on goal and turned inside Pau Cubarsi, Spain’s brilliant young defender. Cubarsi brought him down and the referee pointed to the spot. Cucurella still lay prone. Bellingham, his Real Madrid teammate, leaned over him and told him what he thought of him.

There were a whole host of VAR checks but England passed all of them. The crowd whistled their distaste. Kane missed a penalty in the Wembley game between these two teams in September but he did not miss this one. Simon guessed the right way but Kane hit it too fiercely and it bulged the back of the net. It was his 93rd goal for England.

Spain are not used to being bossed around like this. Tempers flared after the whistle blew for half-time. Ben White and Fabian Ruiz joined in a disagreement of some sort and soon there was a flurry of pushing and shoving. It stopped short of being a melee but it was obvious Spain were shaken.

Eight minutes into the second half, England went further ahead. Rice swung a corner into the centre of the box and, as the usual wrestling match unfolded, Ezri Konsa ran in gloriously unmarked and nodded the ball down and past the helpless Simon from close range.

Four minutes later, against a general backdrop of disbelief, England were three ahead. What a goal it was, too. Bellingham, who had been his usual superhuman self, muscled his way free in the centre and fed the ball out to Kane.

Kane held the ball up and played it back to Bellingham on the edge of the box. Bellingham spotted the overlapping run of White and found him with a clever pass. White took a touch and slotted the ball past Simon. It was the Arsenal full-back’s first competitive England start, too. Maybe now England fans will stop booing him.

This was the night Thomas Tuchel had been crying out for as he got the evidence he demanded.

Ezri Konsa met Declan Rice's set-piece to plant an unstoppable header in the back of the net.

Recent findings suggest that but then, midway through the half, England gave Spain a lifeline. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession by Yamal and as Yamal bore down on goal, Anderson pulled him back. Anderson was shown a red card and Spain were awarded a penalty. Oyarzabal waited for Trafford to commit himself and then stroked the ball into the opposite corner.

Industry observers note that the atmosphere in the stadium was transformed. Spain sensed vulnerability in England for the first time. Fifteen minutes from time, they pulled another goal back. Yamal sprinted away down the right and slid the ball into the middle for substitute Nico Williams, who sidefooted it past Trafford.

Now, it was like the Alamo. Yamal tormented England. Trafford dived at full length to push away one of his shots and then got down at his near post to divert a shot that was creeping in. White produced another of the moments of the night with a flying block to keep out a goalbound shot from Williams.

Industry observers note that spain threw everything at England but England would not yield. When Trafford made that double save, everyone knew. It was to be England’s night. Tuchel had his proof of concept.

According to recent reports, E’ andato in scena la prima edizione del premio “Eccellenza Calcistica Italiana”, riconoscimento dedicato alle figure che hanno lasciato il segno nel panorama calcistico nazionale. Tra i vincitori figura anche il vicepresidente della SSC Napoli, Edoardo De Laurentiis, premiato per i meriti conseguiti nell’area della Governance: “E’ per me un grande onore ricevere questo riconoscimento, ma la gioia è doppia per averlo condiviso con mio padre, che è il mio mentore e la mia guida. Ho mosso i primi passi in questo mondo quando ero ancora molto giovane, ho commesso diversi sbagli, ma mi impegno quotidiano per crescere ed essere all’altezza del mio ruolo”.

Successivamente, a margine della cerimonia di premiazione, il vicepresidente ha aggiunto: “La chiave è proseguire giorno dopo giorno con costanza, facendo gruppo. La coesione è fondamentale per raggiungere gli obiettivi prefissati. Diventerà la futura casa del Napoli (riferendosi al nuovo centro sportivo), un luogo in cui far crescere i giovani, costruire il nostro vivaio e scoprire nuovi talenti. Abbiamo vissuto tantissime esperienze entusiasmanti, dall’era Spalletti fino a Conte. La più grande è stata osservare la squadra capace di conquistare costantemente traguardi prestigiosi e di mantenersi sempre ad altissimi livelli”.

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0.

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

In a recent development, despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

Sources indicate that mcGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo.

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery remarked: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

According to recent reports, “It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”.

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Sources indicate that vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim.

Recent findings suggest that villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today revealed as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of substantial-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s fresh-look crew.

In a recent development, morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

In a recent development, although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#61361. Ashley Cole accidentally shooting a student, bare-chested Marcus Bent threatening police with a meat cleaver - and an ex-Barcelona star firing a gun in a hospital! Footballers' fascination with weapons after Amar Dedic's bow and arrows saga

Ashley Cole accidentally shooting a student, bare-chested Marcus Bent threatening police with a meat cleaver - and an ex-Barcelona star firing a gun in a hospital! Footballers' fascination with weapons after Amar Dedic's bow and arrows saga

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and WILL GOVE.
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Amar Dedic might have fancied himself as Robin Hood – but the Newcastle United defender's latest adventure in the Northumberland countryside led to a rather less merry altercation with police last week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and WILL GOVE.

Published: 07:00 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EST, 16 November 2026.

Amar Dedic might have fancied himself as Robin Hood – but the Newcastle United defender's latest adventure in the Northumberland countryside led to a rather less merry altercation with police last week.

The Magpies star sparked a major police operation after being spotted carrying a bow and arrows near a reservoir outside Newcastle, with at least six patrol cars joining the search for the £30million player.

After tracking down and questioning the Bosnian, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public and that the equipment was intended for recreational use.

But Dedic's escapade was certainly not the first time a footballer has found himself in hot water over the possession, carrying or use of a weapon, with brass knuckles, meat cleavers and BB guns among the bizarre arsenal of items to have attracted the authorities' attention over the years.

Marcus Bent, with a meat cleaver, in Surrey.

Former Middlesbrough and Everton forward Marcus Bent was tasered in his own home by police after threatening armed police officers with a meat cleaver and kitchen knife while under the influence of cocaine.

Bent, who avoided jail in 2016 after he pleaded guilty to possession of cocaine and affray, called Surrey Police after thinking he had discovered an intruder in his home.

Officers arrived at the scene but were initially unable to gain access to the property. Guildford Crown Court heard how the officers were about to use a battering ram to gain entry when a bare-chested Bent 'flung' open the door holding two chef's knives, with his 'eyes wide, jaw clenched and his body rigid'.

Recent findings suggest that bent, who was handed a 12-month sentence, suspended for two years, later noted: 'I was paranoid and I was hallucinating. I felt there were people in my house. I remember thinking the door handle was moving.

Sources indicate that 'At no point was I ever going to take someone's life. I called them because I was hallucinating, paranoid, terrified.'.

Marcus Bent arrives at court before pleading guilty to possession of cocaine and affray.

Ashley Cole, with an air rifle, in Cobham.

To most, Ashley Cole is England's all-time greatest full-back but the three-time Premier League winner also made headlines for an infamous training ground air rifle incident.

Back in 2011 while playing for Chelsea, Ashley Cole accidentally shot and injured 21-year-old student Tom Cowan, who was on work experience at the Blues' training ground in Cobham, Surrey.

The Champions League winning left-back was reportedly 'larking about' with a .22 air rifle and accidentally shot Cowan from just five feet away.

The student had assumed he would get an invaluable experience on his brief visit to Cobham but instead had to be treated by medics and rest for the remainder of the day after the shot was fired.

Cole accidentally shot a 21-year-old on work experience at Chelsea's training ground.

Darren Bent, with a BB Gun, in Kesgrave.

Ex-England star Darren Bent ran into trouble early in his career when he was questioned over the alleged shooting of a 12-year-old boy with a ball-bearing gun.

While starring for his boyhood club Ipswich at the age of 20 in May 2004, Bent was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm with intent to cause violence, before he was placed on bail and eventually released without charge pending further investigations.

Industry observers note that according to a Suffolk Police statement at the time, a 12-year-old boy at a play area in Kesgrave had been struck in the back by a pellet from a ball-bearing gun (BB Gun). The incident was reported to authorities by his mother.

Bent, who was given a formal caution for his actions, went on to enjoy a fruitful career in the Premier League, representing the likes of Charlton, Tottenham, Sunderland and Aston Villa while also winning 13 caps for the Three Lions.

Early on his career Premier League legend Darren Bent was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm.

Karim Adeyemi, with brass knuckles, in Germany.

The only member of this list to still be playing is Germany and Barcelona's Karim Adeyemi who was fined £396,000 in 2025 for possessing a pair of brass knuckles.

The former Borussia Dortmund forward was caught with the knuckles back in 2024, at the age of 22, but had to wait until the following year to receive his punishment.

In a recent development, under German law the possession, procurement and use of brass knuckles is prohibited. The young winger avoided a public trial and a criminal record and was given a fine consisting of 60 daily payments of £6,600.

Although he never used the weapon, the German was in hot water  as he briefly lost his starting place in the German national team and at Borussia Dortmund.

The Westphalia giants released a statement saying: 'BVB always takes criminal allegations seriously and uses them as an opportunity to discuss them with its employees while respecting confidentiality obligations.'.

Adeyemi was lucky to dodge prison time after being charged with the possession of brass knuckles.

Diego Maradona, with an air rifle, in Buenos Aires.

Argentina icon Diego Maradona caused injuries to four people when he fired an air rifle at journalists and photographers while hiding behind a parked Mercedes outside his Buenos Aires home in February 1994.

Four years later, Maradona was found guilty of assault with a weapon and given a suspended prison sentence of two years and ten months, which was later reduced to an even two years.

To many he is the best of all time but Diego Maradona is hardly infallible off the pitch.

Despite appealing against the sentence which they claimed was 'too light', the journalists injured by Maradona said the verdict at least demonstrated there was 'justice for all' in Argentina.

'At least this exemplary case does show that there is justice for all,' stated Daniel Talamoni, one of the four reporters who sued the World Cup winner.

'When the case began four years ago, everyone remarked it was impossible. They would sentence a man idolised in Argentina and forgive everything.'.

Arda Turan, with an unlicensed gun, in a Turkish hospital.

Keen fans of European football will not need to be reminded of who Arda Turan is. But they may be surprised to learn that the former Atletico Madrid and Barcelona star has had some serious trouble with the law.

Turan somehow avoided a jail sentence after discharging an unlicensed firearm in a hospital.

In 2018 while on loan from Barcelona in his home country of Turkey at Istanbul Basaksehir, Turan got into an altercation with Turkish singer Berkay Sahin, who ended in hospital with a broken nose.

Then Turan turned up at the hospital that was treating Sahin with an unlicensed firearm, and fired a shot into the floor.

He was eventually sentenced to two years and eight months behind bars for firing a gun to cause panic, illegal possession of weapons and intentional injury but the sentence was suspended for five years. Basaksehir also fined the midfielder £350,000 over the incident.

Nearly a decade after the incident, Turan now manages Ukrainian powerhouse Shakhtar Donetsk, joining the club in May of last year.

In a recent development, aurelio De Laurentiis, presidente del Napoli, è stato tra i protagonisti della prima edizione del premio “Eccellenza Calcistica Italiana”, manifestazione dedicata alle personalità che si sono distinte nel panorama calcistico nazionale. L’evento si è svolto a Villa Campolieto, a Ercolano, dove il patron azzurro ha ricevuto un riconoscimento nella categoria Fair Play, che vedeva tra i finalisti anche Andrea Belotti e Luca Percassi. Nel corso del suo intervento, De Laurentiis ha parlato anche del film dedicato al Centenario del Napoli: “La sceneggiatura del film del centenario la scrive il qui presente Maurizio de Giovanni. Il calcio in Inghilterra è nato con gli aristocratici. Non era un fatto popolare. Arrivarono a Napoli e iniziarono a giocare con gli scugnizzi. Il 1922 sembrerebbe la vera data, poi procrastinata al 1926 per la nascita del Napoli. Che non si chiama Società Sportiva, ma Calcio Napoli. Questo film è venuto talmente bene che una piattaforma importante come Amazon lo porterà nel mondo. Quando abbiamo vinto lo Scudetto con Conte, ho fatto un film e sono andato a Los Angeles: presi questo cinema e ho fatto questa anteprima dove sono arrivati questi tifosi dall’America. C’erano donne emozionatissime che dicevano di non capire nulla di calcio ma che si sono comunque fatte trascinare. Ho scoperto che a San Pedro ci sono 30mila tifosi del Napoli legati all’isola d’Ischia”.

Sarà Ermanno Feliciani, arbitro della sezione di Teramo, a dirigere Catanzaro-Palermo, gara valida per la 12ª giornata del campionato di Serie B, in programma alle ore 17.15 allo stadio Ceravolo. Una designazione che riporta alla memoria dei rosanero un precedente particolarmente amaro, proprio contro la formazione calabrese.

Feliciani, infatti, era il direttore di gara della semifinale d'andata dei playoff della scorsa stagione, quando il Palermo di Filippo Inzaghi uscì sconfitto per 3-0 sul campo del Catanzaro. Una battuta d'arresto pesante, che compromise seriamente le possibilità dei siciliani di raggiungere la finale e che rappresenta ancora una ferita per l'ambiente rosanero.

Non si tratta, peraltro, dell'unico Catanzaro-Palermo diretto dal fischietto di Teramo. Nella stagione 2024/25, in occasione della gara di campionato, Feliciani aveva arbitrato anche il successo per 1-3 dei siciliani, allora guidati da Alessio Dionisi. Il bilancio complessivo del Palermo con lui resta dunque positivo: sette precedenti, con tre vittorie, tre pareggi e una sola sconfitta, proprio quella della semifinale playoff dello scorso maggio.

Catanzaro-Palermo Direttore di gara: Feliciani Assistenti: Di Giacinto-Galimberti IV° Ufficiale: Allegretta VAR: Piccinini AVAR: Gariglio.

Raffaele De Leonardis: “La Zes, il laghetto, le fake news: tutti i retroscena della trattativa con De Laurentiis per il centro sportivo a Qualiano”

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Un Calcio alla Radio è intervenuto Raffaele De Leonardis (sindaco di Qualiano): “Quali sono i progetti da affiancare al centro sportivo del Napoli?
  • Industry observers note that quanto mi hanno dato fastidio le fake news attorno a questo?
  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Un Calcio alla Radio è intervenuto Raffaele De Leonardis (sindaco di Qualiano): “Quali sono i progetti da affiancare al centro sportivo del Napoli? Dopo la firma ho già pensato a cosa fare attorno alla zona. Quella sarà una cittadella dello sport, perché affianco ai terreni dove sorgerà il centro sportivo c’è uno stadio, ci sono campi da tennis e abbiamo in animo un palazzetto dello sport e una piscina. Oggi c’è la parte più difficile, quella della burocrazia e infrastrutture. In poco tempo che mi rimane come sindaco mi metterò a disposizione. Quante volte è saltata la trattativa con il Napoli e perché? La prima volta è saltata per il prezzo d’acquisto. Il Presidente De Laurentiis doveva valutare l’investimento. I primi terreni con destinazione urbanistica si parlava di 100 euro a metro quadro. Non c’era bisogno della Zes. Servivano 20 milioni di euro. Non era nelle disponibilità e intenzioni della società. Perché poi bisognava costruire il centro. E comparando con il Viola Park, finanziato dal 20% del Coni, ci fu un primo stop. Successivamente, la Zes paventava di superare vincoli urbanistici, allora si è cominciato a parlare di terreni agricoli. E quindi si è riallacciato il rapporto perché c’erano terreni che rientravano nei desideri della SSC Napoli. C’è stata una visita, sotto la pioggia, il famoso 30 marzo dell’anno dello Scudetto. Il Presidente del Napoli mi invitò allo stadio Maradona, vidi Massimo Boldi, c’era Serena Brancale, c’era De Martino. Quanti vaffa mi sono preso dal Presidente? Abbastanza (sorride ndr). Nell’ultima riunione c’era Chiavelli, c’erano Testa, Discepolo, c’era anche Edo e lì ho capito che forse c’eravamo. Se De Laurentiis si è messo in auto per vedere le distanze dalle stazioni ai terreni? Sì, la prima volta che venne a visitare i terreni prima di Napoli-Milan fece questo percorso in auto. Il Presidente De Laurentiis chiedeva quanto distasse dalla stazione di Afragola, ed erano circa 20 minuti, dalla stazione di Ponte Riccio al centro sono 10 minuti a piedi e da Varcaturo o zone residenziali dei giocatori sono 8 minuti di auto e dallo stadio sono 20 minuti con la tangenziale. Dall’aeroporto ancora meno, 12-13 minuti. De Laurentiis percepiva che la posizione era buona. Fece però un passo indietro in merito alla storia dei rifiuti tossici, si era spaventato, ma non era vero.

Industry observers note that quanto mi hanno dato fastidio le fake news attorno a questo? No, sono il Sindaco di Qualiano, ne sento tante. Però penso che ci sono solo pensieri in negativo. Ma pensiamo anche in positivo. Tutte queste problematiche potrebbero nascere, magari con la Zes. Ma noi che ci guadagniamo? Niente! C’è uno strumento di legge, sono stati fatti i migliori investimenti, noi stiamo sperando che non venga approvato? De Laurentiis ha firmato un atto notarile, un preliminare condizionato e se arriva l’autorizzazione, si trasforma automaticamente in definitivo. Lui che se ne fa di un terreno agricolo!? La Zes ha sette linee guida. Una delle linee riguarda l’attività produttiva per quanto riguarda turismo e sport. Noi non ci opporremo, perché sarebbe da folli. Chiederemo le infrastrutture che dovranno essere realizzate e aiuteremo il Napoli a realizzarle. Noi stiamo rispettando la legge. Se il prof Discepolo presenta il progetto definitivo in 10-15 giorni e partono i 90 giorni della Zes, seguiremo il countdown. Sentivo parlare di un’autorizzazione preliminare per il muro di cinta, con autorizzazione dei proprietari. Se ci sarà un laghetto? Non so se è un vezzo, ma servirà per irrigare i campi. Sarà a mo’ di cisterna. Se ci saranno hotel? Ci saranno sicuramente le stanze per i giocatori. De Laurentiis tiene tanto alla cantera, penso che farà anche un convitto per i giovani”.
