📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The future of Virgil van Dijk continues to be a much-discussed talking point going into the winter months.

The legendary Liverpool captain will see his current contract expire next June as things stand, with the Dutchman on track to become a free agent just before his 36th birthday.

Transfer insider Graeme Bailey recently claimed that there’s a strong chance of the veteran defender being offered at least a 12-month extension at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola unsurprisingly keen to keep hold of his skipper.

In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele reported of fervent interest from Serie A in Van Dijk amid ongoing speculation over the centre-back’s future.

The journalist wrote: ‘One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides.

‘Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are mentioned to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.’.

While the Rossoneri appear determined to pounce on any uncertainty over Van Dijk’s future, Steele added that the 35-year-old is ‘keen’ to extend his contract at Liverpool.

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Any reports of interest in the Dutchman from other clubs will naturally trigger a level of concern among Reds supporters, but it’s natural that there’d be a queue of suitors for one of the best defenders of his (perhaps any) generation when he’s seven months away from becoming a free agent.

It has been revealed that until such time that a final decision is communicated by LFC, fans’ nerves will be frayed as to Van Dijk’s future. When we’ve already seen Mo Salah and Andy Robertson depart this year, the loss of another modern-day great in 2027 would represent a further gut punch for Kopites.

However, it’s worth remembering that when the Liverpool captain last penned a newly introduced contract in April 2025, he was just over two months away from leaving on a free, so he won’t panic even if there might be considerable gnashing of teeth outside of those involved in negotiations over his future.

James Pearce recently advised Reds supporters not to expect a ‘quick resolution’ over the defender’s situation, so for now, it seems that the best way for Van Dijk to secure a upcoming deal at Anfield is to maintain the strong performance levels he’s shown so far this season.

The noise over his future is sure to continue for the time being, but we remain confident that everything will come together in due course and that our iconic number 4 will continue to grace the famous red shirt in the 2027/28 campaign.

Blackburn Rovers sweat over key duo’s availability against Burnley, but influential star is set to return

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, blackburn Rovers face rivals Burnley on Sunday, and the major story leading up to the game has been Tony Mowbray’s withdrawal from head coach duties due to health issues.
  • It has been revealed that as relayed by local reporter Elliott Jackson, Johnson revealed that star striker Andri Gudjohnsen and midfield mainstay Sam Morsy are alongside Scott Wharton in requiring assessment before the game.
  • One man whose fate has already been confirmed is Balazs Toth, after the goalkeeper broke a finger while away with Hungary.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, blackburn Rovers face rivals Burnley on Sunday, and the major story leading up to the game has been Tony Mowbray’s withdrawal from head coach duties due to health issues. Damien Johnson is stepping into the role in the interim, and he and the first-team staff have a handful of injuries to deal with.

It has been revealed that as relayed by local reporter Elliott Jackson, Johnson revealed that star striker Andri Gudjohnsen and midfield mainstay Sam Morsy are alongside Scott Wharton in requiring assessment before the game. All other players returning from international duty – Tom Atcheson, Augustus Kargbo and Kristi Montgomery – will be tested as well, Johnson has said.

One man whose fate has already been confirmed is Balazs Toth, after the goalkeeper broke a finger while away with Hungary. In better news though, Japanese playmaker Ryoya Morishita has trained over the break and is expected to be available.

Among those requiring assessment, there are some crucial Blackburn Rovers players.

Striker Gudjohnsen is perhaps the most vital player in blue and white halves at the moment. The Icelandic talisman is in unassailable form, with 11 goals in 15 club games alongside four in two while away with his national side over the latest international break.

Industry observers note that morsy has become an influential player since his summer arrival. It perhaps wasn’t expected that he would become such a key starter, but his partnership in midfield with Montgomery has given this Rovers side some experience and bite. Ahead of a high-stakes game with aggression and tough tackles expected, having the Egyptian in the middle of the park will be key.

Toth is a big loss though, so it will be down to Aynsley Pears to step in. Sunday would have been a fitting game for Blackburn-born favourite Wharton to return, but there is understandable patience over his comeback.

Morishita’s return is a big boost, however. The 29-year-old is a key creative source, and even if he can only play from the bench, he can still make a telling impact.

Now, there’s no reason to doubt Johnson’s update, but sections of the Blackburn Rovers support will be hoping that there isn’t as much doubt surrounding the likes of Gudjohnsen and Morsy as has been let on.

Recent findings suggest that indecisive answers on their availability keep Burnley guessing. The rigorous preparation clubs go through before games nowadays means the Clarets will be prepared for all outcomes, but the uncertainty means they have to stay on their toes and proposal carefully for all potential lineups.

One thing for sure is that all of Rovers’ doubts will be doing whatever they can to be fit for the fixture. Not only is this a great chance to end a 16-year wait for an East Lancashire derby win, but the players and staff will be determined to deliver a result for Mowbray after he stepped back earlier this week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 19 Nov 2026 09:26, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 09:34.

Newcastle United fresh boy Matias Fernandez-Pardo could be given a shot from the first whistle in Saturday's Premier League clash with champions Arsenal at St James' Park.

The 21-year-old's start to life in England has been disrupted by a nasty illness, but he was fit enough to come off the bench in Newcastle's 1-1 draw with Fulham two weekends ago.

Matthias Jaissle gave Yoane Wissa the nod in the number 10 role, but the DR Congo man failed to convince, so Fernandez-Pardo could be offered a route back into the first XI.

The former Lille man, also linked with Arsenal during the summer, is expected to join forces with Jacob Murphy, Harvey Barnes and Will Osula in the final third, the former holding off Anthony Elanga after scoring a stunning opening goal at Craven Cottage.

Both Nico Gonzalez and Joe Willock have also battled back from bugs, but the latter is not anticipated to earn a start against his former employers, as fan favourite Sean Steur pairs up with Gonzalez once more.

Lukas Hornicek was Newcastle's saviour in the capital two weekends ago, and the number one should be shielded by an identical backline of Amar Dedic, Malick Thiaw, Dan Burn and Lewis Hall here.

Joelinton and Ewen Jaouen remain out for the Magpies as they recuperate from hamstring injuries.

Newcastle United possible starting lineup:.

Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Burn, Hall; Steur, Gonzalez; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Osula.

By Ben Knapton | 19 Nov 2026 09:34, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 11:51.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has critical attacking and defensive calls to make for Saturday's Premier League clash with Newcastle United at St James' Park.

The Gunners came out of the international break largely unscathed, although Martin Zubimendi will be absent for a few weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem in Spain's 3-2 defeat to England.

However, Zubimendi was never likely to push for a place in the starting lineup in the North East, where Bruno Guimaraes is expected to start against his former club, joining forces with the ever-present Declan Rice.

The pair will line up behind an identical supporting cast of Martin Odegaard, Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke, who continues to deputise effectively for the injured Bukayo Saka and suspended Max Dowman.

Viktor Gyokeres extended an all-time Nations League record during the international break, but the Swede should still lose out to Arteta favourite Kai Havertz for a start in the number nine slot.

Arteta faces a similar dilemma in defence, where William Saliba is once again fit and available, but the in-form Ezri Konsa has done nothing to warrant demotion.

As a result, the champions should deploy an identical backline to the one that started the 1-0 win over Hull City two weekends ago, as Jurrien Timber also keeps Ben White at bay.

Arsenal possible starting lineup:.

Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

Tech Report: Burnley team news and predicted XI to face Blackburn Rovers as key player returns for derby day

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (677 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fabio Celestini has inherited a sinking ship with the monumental task of keeping Burnley afloat, with the international break arriving at the perfect time to put a temporary halt to their struggle.
  • The Clarets’ 5-4 capitulation at Cardiff City, where they were leading 4-1 by the 62nd minute, was a brutal reminder of where they find themselves.
  • As it stands, Burnley sit 22nd in the Championship table with just one win in 15 games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabio Celestini has inherited a sinking ship with the monumental task of keeping Burnley afloat, with the international break arriving at the perfect time to put a temporary halt to their struggle.

The Clarets’ 5-4 capitulation at Cardiff City, where they were leading 4-1 by the 62nd minute, was a brutal reminder of where they find themselves. Celestini’s squad are devoid of confidence and leaking goals at will.

As it stands, Burnley sit 22nd in the Championship table with just one win in 15 games. They are already five points from safety and lurking in the bottom three alongside Derby County and Preston North End.

Blackburn Rovers meanwhile will feel they can finally end their 16-year wait for a victory over their arch rivals, buoyed by a 2-1 victory over promotion-chasing West Ham last time out.

Anel Ahmedhodzic could return to the fold having missed the trip to Cardiff City due to illness, but Conor Roberts will be absent after a red card in South Wales and will serve the first match of his three-game suspension.

Injuries have been an unfortunate feature of Dastan Satpayev’s time at Turf Moor since arriving on loan from Chelsea and he remains out with a recurring hamstring issue. Tunisian international Hannibal Mejbri will be absent with the same injury.

The defeat at Lincoln City brought an end to Nicky Hayen’s time in charge, and it also brought Amando Broja’s season to a temporary standstill with a groin injury. Fellow frontman Ashley Barnes remains out, but is nearing a return after featuring for the U21s side.

It has been revealed that jacob Bruun Larsen is out due to a stress fracture and Jordan Beyer remains a long-term absentee and is yet to make a competitive appearance since December 2023 due to a serious knee injury. Among those also unavailable are Ben Amos, Mike Tresor, Shurandy Sambo and Michael Obafemi.

Recent findings suggest that in better news, Bashir Humphreys has been back in training and is on the brink of a return. The Blackburn Rovers clash may come too soon, but he could return next week.

Coudert; Walker, Ahmedhodzic, Ekdal, Pires; Cullen, Hatate; Ramazani, Edwards, Banel; Vardy.

Recent findings suggest that due to injuries, Celestini’s side pretty much picks for itself. However, there could be one key change in midfield.

Gregoire Coudert has only kept two clean sheets this term, but will line up between the sticks.

Gregoire Coudert’s Burnley stats.

The full-back flanks will be occupied by Kyle Walker on the right and Lucas Pires on the left, while the returning Ahmedhodzic could partner Hjalmar Ekdal at centre-back in place of Igor Julio.

Josh Laurent and Reo Hatate have been the midfield pivot for the last two outings, but after three appearances off the bench, club captain and star player Josh Cullen could return to the starting lineup for the first time since his ACL injury in December 2025.

In a recent development, marcus Edwards plays in attacking midfield, and with two goals in three games under Celestini, the right-wing position will likely fall to the in-form Largie Ramazani. Jayden Banel plays off the left.

The centre-forward spot is the one position which is up for grabs, with Andreas Hountondji beginning to show signs of promise. However, the experience of Jamie Vardy could prove crucial in a game of this significance.

Burnley vs Blackburn Rovers kicks off at 12:00 on Sunday, and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Football and ITV.

#61260. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

📅 09 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 23m • 📚 Deep Dive (4628 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4628 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.
  • Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.
  • Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Recent findings suggest that palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

Recent findings suggest that when it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”.

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Recent findings suggest that palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

Recent findings suggest that it looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as massive of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Industry observers note that cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

Recent findings suggest that “Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, noted. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”.

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

It has been revealed that reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Recent findings suggest that reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who remarked: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

Industry observers note that “I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”.

Industry observers note that goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk.

Sources indicate that but the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Industry observers note that valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav.

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were rapidly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

On the defeat by Chelsea, Farke noted: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”.

According to recent reports, "100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers notes he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla.

In a recent development, here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

According to recent reports, TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

It has been revealed that "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

Asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he stated: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”.

It has been revealed that on Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady stated on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the big guns came on... They were electric at times.”.

A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

Fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

Recent findings suggest that rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

Sources indicate that chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

In a recent development, shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

Sources indicate that leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

According to recent reports, valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

We could be in for a blockbuster finish.

Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

Industry observers note that it will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

Industry observers note that palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

Industry observers note that chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

Chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

In a recent development, chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

It has been revealed that chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Industry observers note that chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav.

Alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

Industry observers note that substantial cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:.

In a recent development, boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

In a recent development, there is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

Sources indicate that better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

Industry observers note that gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

In a recent development, gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

It has been revealed that farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

It has been revealed that big chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

Leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu rolls out a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

According to recent reports, barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

Industry observers note that there is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as massive as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

Major chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

Recent findings suggest that gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

According to recent reports, leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

According to recent reports, although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Sources indicate that asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke said: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

It has been revealed that “We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few upcoming players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”.

According to recent reports, tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard noted of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”.

Your Blues to face Leeds United in the #CarabaoCup! #CFC pic.twitter.com/636SOiUXVB.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

Sources indicate that in Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

According to recent reports, alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 11:15.
  • Aiming to further strengthen their survival bid, Notts County welcome playoff-chasing Stevenage to Meadow Lane for an all-crucial League One clash on Saturday afternoon.
  • The Magpies enjoyed a promising unbeaten run prior to the November international break, whilst the Boro also experienced success in both the FA Cup and EFL Trophy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 11:15.

Aiming to further strengthen their survival bid, Notts County welcome playoff-chasing Stevenage to Meadow Lane for an all-crucial League One clash on Saturday afternoon.

The Magpies enjoyed a promising unbeaten run prior to the November international break, whilst the Boro also experienced success in both the FA Cup and EFL Trophy.

For the first time since the 2014-15 campaign, Notts County are back in the third tier of English football, with the East Midlanders aiming to avoid a season of bottom-four struggle in League One.

Since a 2-0 defeat by Wycombe Wanderers on October 17, the Magpies have strung together a five-game unbeaten run (W4 D1) across third tier, FA Cup and EFL Trophy action, including a 3-0 away success at Burton Albion in the latter competition on November 10.

After collecting a commendable tally of seven points from their past three third-tier contests, Notts County have moved up to 18th position in the League One standings, two points above the relegation spaces.

A worrying statistic ahead of Saturday afternoon, only Peterborough United (5), Barnsley (5) and whipping boys Bromley (5) have earned fewer than the Magpies' eight home points in the division so far.

Head coach Martin Paterson was heralded as a hero after guiding Notts County to League Two playoff victory during this first campaign in charge, however, the former Tampa Bay Rowdies assistant now faces a different type of task at a higher level of the English pyramid.

Just days before the announcement of his contract extension, Stevenage captain Carl Piergianni netted the only goal of the Kassam Stadium contest to knock Oxford United out of the FA Cup at the first-round stage.

At the beginning of the following week, the Boro enjoyed an EFL Trophy win over Fulham Under-21s, meaning that Alex Revell's troops were three games unbeaten (W2 D1) across all competitions heading into the November pause.

Stevenage were losing semi-finalists to Stockport County in last season's playoffs, and the Hertfordshire outfit are right now way off the top-six pace, sitting seven points behind sixth-placed Plymouth Argyle.

Following Jamie Reid's summer switch to divisional rivals Reading, the Boro have shared the goalscoring responsibilities amongst their ranks, with Dan Kemp, Josh Magennis and Oliver Sanderson all netting on three occasions in League One so far.

Due to Notts County's recent plights in non-league and League Two, Saturday's meeting at Meadow Lane will be the first between the two sides since March 2019, with the Magpies unbeaten in their past four battles (W2 D2) against Stevenage dating back to November 2017.

Notts County form (all competitions):.

Stevenage form (all competitions):.

Both returning from international duty with Republic of Ireland Under-21s, Darius Lipsiuc and Rory Finneran could feature this weekend for Notts County.

Back from two substitute appearances for Sierra Leone in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying, Charlton Athletic loanee Daniel Kanu is looking for his seventh League One start of the term.

Nicholas Tsaroulla has spent time away on Nations League duty for Cyprus and could be an option in the middle of the park or at wing-back for the Magpies at Meadow Lane.

Scoring for Stevenage in the most recent league match at Leicester City on October 31, Ben Broggio and Tugra Turhan are pushing for starts.

There is still plenty of experience within the Boro ranks, though, with Northern Irishman Magennis and midfielder Louis Thompson expected to make the XI.

Notts County possible starting lineup:.

Belshaw; Ness, McDonald, Bedeau; Tsaroulla, Finneran, Robertson, Samuels-Smith; Roberts; Kanu, Smyth.

Stevenage possible starting lineup:.

Setford; Vancooten, Casey, Piergianni, Earley; Sanderson, Thompson, Phillips, Patterson; Broggio; Magennis.

Unbeaten against Stevenage since March 2017, Notts County should be confident of extending their positive run at Meadow Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Boro have won just one of their opening six away league trips this term and are likely to struggle in the East Midlands.

By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026.

Next week Arsene Wenger will be in Qatar for the second staging of FIFA's 48-team Under-17 World Cup.

It has been revealed that he described last year's inaugural event using one evocative word. 'Paradise,' he said. 'Basically, 25 per cent of the football world was here.'.

At the end of last month – as the fall-out from FIFA president Gianni Infantino's foiled strategy to sell off parts of the men's senior World Cup rumbled on – Wenger was in Azerbaijan at the hosting of the very first Under-15 version.

Industry observers note that an eight-a-side tournament with the emphasis on technique and quality, it was – in his role as FIFA's head of global development – another of his own ideas. According to those who know him, this is Wenger's happy place.

'Arsene's vision is very simple,' one long-time ally tells Daily Mail Sport. 'It has always been that as many boys and girls as possible can participate in the game under as good a quality of coaching as is physically and financially possible.

'That is it, basically. That is why he works for FIFA. He wants that direct influence on the game. He is 77 but fundamentally he is a coach at heart. In his own mind, he still has his whistle in his mouth and his stopwatch round his wrist.'.

It has been revealed that arsene Wenger is FIFA's head of global development and many thought he'd challenge Gianni Infantino for the presidency of the organisation. Those hopes were misplaced.

Wenger, the former Arsenal manager, is still a coach at heart according to those that know him well.

According to recent reports, viewed in this context, it is perhaps not a surprise that Wenger is no longer expected to stand as a rival to Infantino at next March's presidential elections in Rabat. The deadline for nominations is on Wednesday.

According to recent reports, wenger's fury at what he saw as Infantino's World Cup treachery was limitless. Some close to him feared he may quit in protest at an organisation he joined seven years ago. Others urged him to challenge Infantino's presidency, hoping it would serve to cleanse FIFA's reputation for sleaze.

But even though as recently as last week Wenger's intentions remained unclear to many people within the organisation, the conflict raging inside his own head was crystal clear.

'Arsene is an idealist and a romantic,' explains another source who has known him for 20 years. 'And the head of that organisation is not a place for someone like that. FIFA presidency is about glad-handing and politics and – let's face it – money.

Sources indicate that 'Say what you like about Infantino, he's good at it. It's his natural habitat. He knows the rules. Arsene? He would lie awake at night wondering where all the money was going. He would be fretting about whether it was being spent in all the areas the different confederations told him it was.

'On the one hand, Arsene would be a perfect figurehead for the global game. A purist. The total antithesis to Infantino's perceived chicanery. But in reality, how much could he change? Many of FIFA's reputational issues are deeply embedded.'.

The sub-plot to Wenger's emotional conflict regarding a direct challenge to Infantino is that inside FIFA it has had an all or nothing feel to it. The former Arsenal manager's contract in his current global development role expires at the end of this year and for all that the organisation would very much like him to renew, there remains the possibility that he may walk away.

If Wenger doesn't – as we now expect – stand in opposition to Infantino, will he have the appetite to continue working underneath him?

Wenger was furious with Infantino's foiled blueprint to sell off parts of the men's senior World Cup.

Sources indicate that wenger with the Premier League trophy in 2004. 'Arsene would be a perfect figurehead for the global game. A purist,' indicates a source who knows him well.

In a recent development, wenger, for example, was a noticeable absentee when other FIFA leaders gathered to support Infantino at a management committee meeting in Morocco in August. The two men were not seen together again until they stood side by side at the Under-15 tournament last month.

Sources indicate that 'I think that (Wenger's future) is a very pertinent question,' adds another ally. 'It's on his mind and it's a massive decision. To a much lesser degree, his age may well be a factor too. But he has the fire in his belly. He has energy. I know that.

Sources indicate that 'He had a certain aim and certain targets when he started with FIFA. And he hasn't met them yet.'.

Under Wenger's stewardship and guidance, FIFA have established 60 academies in previously under-resourced football backwaters such as India, Uzbekistan and Fresh Caledonia.

Recent findings suggest that 'We provide the structure, the finance and – by way of top coaches – the expertise,' explains a source from the governing body. 'For example, we have Spanish coaches leading the way in India. We basically have coaches coaching the coaches, if that makes sense.

'Arsene believes every child in the world should have a pathway if they have the talent. India, for example, have never been to a senior men's World Cup. Arsene wants to change that.'.

At last month's Under-15 World Cup, 500 players were involved who had emerged from Wenger's FIFA academies. The governing body's stated aim is to have established 75 by the end of next year.

'In Arsene's mind, the number would actually be 100,' laughs his associate. 'And he knows he isn't there yet.'.

Spain, watched by Infantino (left), raise the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan last month.

The Under-15 World Cup was one of Wenger's ideas and is an eight-a-side tournament with the emphasis on technique and quality.

Wenger is evangelical about it all. Some would – and do – say he remains a dreamer at heart. He also remains a small details person. For example, the reason he has established the Under-17 World Cup as an annual event is that he doesn't want a single talented footballer to fall through the cracks and miss out simply by being born a year too early or too late.

The Frenchman is not, however, without his contradictions. Once asked privately how a father of a daughter could justify a FIFA decision to hold the 2034 World Cup in Saudi Arabia – where the women's rights problem remains deeply contentious – Wenger suggested that he wished only to 'effect change from within'.

According to recent reports, just as pertinent is the impact Wenger has undoubtedly had – for better or for worse – on football's global calendar. You don't have to have a particularly sharp memory to recall the many times Wenger railed against the dangers of too much travel and playing-time on his top players when he was in charge at Arsenal.

Of all the top English clubs, Arsenal were the last to commit to arduous pre-season tours to places like America and the Far East and that was simply because Wenger was the manager. He always preferred a week in the Austrian mountains to a schlep round the world.

Now – eight-and-a-half years on from his departure from the Emirates – Wenger has been firmly attached to FIFA's gravy train for some time, a driving force behind the expanded summer Club World Cup and a key advocate of a strategy to hold the World Cup every two years that ultimately didn't get off the ground.

In a recent development, wenger is on record on the matter. 'The welfare of the players in the last 20 years has increased dramatically,' Wenger has said. 'When you look at injury prevention, recovery work, nutrition and advances in medical technology. It is unrecognisable from what it used to be.

'Also VAR has helped with the protection of players, as players know they cannot escape from making bad tackles that cause injury.'.

Recent findings suggest that club coaches across Europe may raise eyebrows at that. So would many of those who opposed the expansion of this year's World Cup to 48 teams. But alternative theories are also in play.

Asked how a father of a daughter could justify the decision to hold the 2034 World Cup in Saudi Arabia – where women's rights are deeply contentious – Wenger noted he only wished to 'effect change from within'.

Many wanted Wenger to challenge Infantino's presidency, hoping it would serve to cleanse FIFA's reputation for sleaze.

In a recent development, 'Arsene was seen as poster boy for the two-year World Cup and, yes, he put his weight behind it,' explains our FIFA source. 'But in truth we were being asked that question by some member associations. It was FIFA's duty to look into it.

According to recent reports, 'The mistake some people make is to look at everything from a European perspective. European football is blessed but not everybody is. Many countries just don't play as much competitive football and Arsene is strong on the global view.

In a recent development, 'He listened to the pushback but wants to give opportunities to clubs from smaller nations in things like the Club World Cup and a bigger World Cup. It's not just about England, France, Germany, Argentina and Brazil.

Recent findings suggest that 'When you are a club manager you are paid to be essentially selfish and when he looks back he recognises that. His horizons have been broadened. Some of the smaller nations don't have the calendar congestion that exists in England, for example. His principles remain the same but he has just seen another perspective.'.

In a recent development, by his own self-effacing admission, Wenger has always led a rather monastic existence. Splitting his time between Zurich – where FIFA have their HQ – and his home in the north London enclave of Totteridge, he still endeavours to run 5km every morning. After that, it's football.

In a recent development, 'If there is football on TV from one of the leagues then I will watch it,' he told Mo Farah on a recent episode of the Olympic Champion's podcast. 'It's simply what I like to do.'.

It is not too simplistic to say that the sport remains Wenger's obsession. It is hard to imagine him without it at the core of his life. Equally, it is difficult to imagine a return to club football in any meaningful capacity.

The wounds caused by what he felt was a rancorous departure from Arsenal have healed but that, nevertheless, remains a chapter closed.

'Arsene was seen as poster boy for the two-year World Cup and, yes, he put his weight behind it,' explains our FIFA source.

'Sir Alex Ferguson was capable of staying tight to Manchester United but for Arsene and Arsenal it was different'.

'It would be disingenuous to say it wasn't all a bit distant and uncomfortable for a while,' indicates a source with knowledge of the situation. 'Arsene made a decision to step away from it completely. Sir Alex Ferguson was capable of staying tight to Manchester United but for Arsene and Arsenal it was different.

According to recent reports, 'The ending was different for a start. So it was a bit like a divorce. You need some distance for a while before you can remember what you liked about each other back in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that 'But that's where it is now. It's thawed. There is semi-regular contact. He's been back to a game, even if it was just the one.'.

According to recent reports, for Wenger, the pull of what he sees as unfinished business with FIFA may remain strong. Equally, beyond the rather waspish and phlegmatic public face has always run a river of steel.

'You don't go toe to toe with Fergie all of those years and have all that personal c**p poured on you by Jose Mourinho and come out the other side in one piece if you haven't got some proper b***s,' says one of our sources.

Recent findings suggest that 'Some of us were surprised how long it took him to come out and speak publicly about his opposition to Infantino's World Cup sell-off. It was discussed. But he got there in the end. The bottom line is that he has his principles and he already has his relevance. Infantino constantly has to fight for his. Arsene does not. If he isn't comfortable where he works, he will always find something else.'.

Recent findings suggest that it's a view thoroughly endorsed by just about everybody in Wenger's orbit. 'Whatever he does next – whether with FIFA or somewhere else – it will be in football,' adds an ally. 'The next chapter will be his decision. He is very focused. And there is already a legacy.'.

According to recent reports, 'The bottom line is that Wenger has his principles and he already has his relevance. Infantino constantly has to fight for his'.

Wenger and Infantino will in all likelihood be side by side in Doha next week as the second staging of FIFA's 48-team Under-17 World Cup gets into full swing.

Industry observers note that wenger and Infantino will in all likelihood be side by side in Doha next week as the Under-17 jamboree gets into full swing. Teams from Tanzania, Mozambique and Vietnam will make their debut in the 104-match tournament. In Qatar, FIFA will present a thoroughly united front with Wenger's avowed principles at its core.

'You can play with an orange or you can make a ball with paper,' Wenger told The Independent in a rare interview three years ago. 'That's why football is so popular. But today if you want to get to a good level of education in football, in some countries you don't get it.

'I find that not right because, in many countries, there are some private initiatives, but the parents have to pay to get the children in there and play. For me, it doesn't matter if you're rich or poor. If you are good, you come in.

It has been revealed that 'Our academies are free, just open to talent. You have to adapt and find a solution in every country.'.

Industry observers note that wolves host Charlton Athletic this weekend as they look to go top of the Championship table with a win. Cesar Peixoto’s side are presently 4th in the table but are just one point behind Birmingham City, Middlesbrough and Stoke City ahead of them.

Ahead of the Charlton clash, Peixoto has been speaking to The Express and Star providing a full upgrade on his squad. The Wolves boss had plenty of positive news, including that Fer Lopez is closing in on a return to full fitness.

“Fer did not train in the first week (of the international break) because he was recovering from injury.” mentioned Peixoto. “Fer had a good week of training. We had to manage him on Thursday, but he trained well and needed this kind of training with the team.

Sources indicate that “Fer is not 100 per cent. He has a little pain, but nothing crucial at this stage. But we are going to see a better Fer, because when he came back from the previous international break he was injured and played with pain.

According to recent reports, “We have to manage the minutes with him. He is an important player for us. But I think he will be better than before.”.

Peixoto also mentioned that Jean-Ricner Bellegarde and Jordan James have trained on Thursday and Friday but are not 100%. On another positive note, Bertrand Traore and Boubacar Traore have returned to full training.

Lopez has emerged as one of Wolves’ most influential players this season, with the 22-year-old making an impressive impact following his return from a loan spell at Celta Vigo.

The Spanish attacking midfielder has scored six goals and provided three assists in 14 Championship appearances, accumulating 1,097 minutes and an average rating of 7.58, according to FotMob. He has also contributed a goal in the Carabao Cup, taking his overall return to seven goals and three assists in 16 appearances.

Recent findings suggest that the summer 2025 signing has become a key figure under Peixoto, helping Wolves climb to fourth in the Championship with 28 points from 15 matches. His return from a loan spell at Celta Vigo has proved particularly valuable, with Wolves now targeting an immediate return to the Premier League.

Sources indicate that lopez’ return is a massive plus for Wolves, however they need to wary with him. The Spaniard has already picked up several knocks in this campaign, which will be a concern,.

Peixoto is clearly aware of the need to careful with him and will want to protect him this season. So far this campaign they have got away with him just picking up the odd short-term concern but if they keep persisting he will suffer a long-term problem, which would be a massive concern for Wolves this season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 11:20, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:20.

Real Madrid will be aiming to continue their excellent run of form when they resume their La Liga campaign against Celta Vigo on Saturday night.

Los Blancos have been victorious in each of their last eight matches in all competitions, including a 3-0 success over Valencia before the November international break.

Jose Mourinho's side are at the moment second in the La Liga table, three points behind the leaders Barcelona, boasting a record of 10 wins and two draws from their 12 league matches during the 2026-27 campaign.

Celta, meanwhile, have a record of two wins, seven draws and three defeats from their 12 games during the current season.

The Vigo outfit are currently 11th in the division on 13 points.

Here, Sports Mole looks at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Real Madrid and Celta ahead of their clash in the Spanish capital this weekend.

These two sides have locked horns on 139 occasions throughout history, and Real Madrid comfortably lead the head-to-head record, having won 83 times to Celta's 35, while there have also been 21 draws.

Real Madrid have netted 324 times against Celta, conceding 175, while Cristiano Ronaldo is the all-time leading goalscorer in this fixture, having scored 20 goals against the Sky Blues during his time with Los Blancos.

Unsurprisingly, Real Madrid have also dominated their La Liga meetings, winning 73 of their 120 matches, suffering 30 defeats in the process, while there have been 17 draws.

Notably, three of Celta's last four wins over Real Madrid have actually come at the Bernabeu, while they have only beaten Los Blancos once in front of their own supporters since May 2001.

Real enjoyed a 10-game winning run against Celta in La Liga between May 2014 and December 2025, when Os Celestes emerged 2-0 winners in the Spanish capital during their most recent clash at Bernabeu.

Xabi Alonso's side came into that game desperate to keep up with Barcelona in the title race, but after conceding the first goal to Williot Swedberg's brilliant flick early in the second half, frustrations grew.

Madrid left-back Fran Garcia picked up two yellow cards in around sixty seconds shortly beyond the hour mark, before Alvaro Fernandez Carreras saw a straight red for abusing the referee in stoppage time.

To make matters worse, Swedberg then added a second when he was played through by Celta legend Iago Aspas and dribbled around Thibaut Courtois before walking the ball into an empty net.

However, Real Madrid were able to gain some revenge in the reverse meeting in Vigo in March 2026, with the capital giants recording a last-gasp 2-1 in.

Celta will now be aiming to make it back-to-back wins over Real Madrid at Bernabeu.
